newsitem.title: UK: LME base metal prices wind up weaker in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: LME base metal prices wind up weaker in thin trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices tumbled in afternoon trading on Wedensday, tailed by the rest of the base metals.
Flagship copper had started drifting lower early in the day after a strong pre-market failed to translate into follow-through buying in the rings, traders said.
Prices then dipped steeply in the afternoon amid general light selling in thin conditions, they added.
"The market took an easier turn this afternoon. After copper failed to break above $2,285 it came lower on light selling and hit some sell stops," a trader said.
News that Chile's largest copper mine Escondida said a planned strike would not hurt output may also have accelerated the decline, traders said.
But the fact that only a small group of unionized workers, or 17 percent of the workforce, planned to strike meant the effect was minimal one way or another, one added.
Amid the recent thin volumes, copper was range trading in a broader $2,240-$2,295 band, with little conviction on the upside or downside, he added.
Three months metal ended the afternoon kerb at $2,256, down $22 from Tuesday's kerb close.
Some support was expected to emerge at the psychological $2,250 level and then $2,245, the low from Monday, traders said.
Despite the decline, cash to threes backwardation was largely steady at $35/$37.
Nickel was also sharply lower at $7,255, a decline of $145 from Tuesday, after an attempt to regain the $7,400 level lost steam.
Aluminium was less affected by the afternoon selling, although it also ended the afternoon kerb $8 lower at $1,547. Like copper, it had failed an upside bid and came lower.
Lead and zinc suffered a worse blow, however, after a halfhearted stab at the upside failed in the morning despite Tuesday's positive kerb closes.
"Volumes are so thin that any business coming through will move prices higher or lower,"
Lead finished $6 softer at $639, while zinc settled $18 weaker at $1,241.
Tin also ended lower at $5,690, a decline of $70, after a steady start to the day.
Alloy was virtually unchanged at $1,448/50, from $1,450/55.
